newsitem.title: UK: Barclays looking for capital return method.
newsitem.headline: Barclays looking for capital return method.

text.p: Barclays chief executive Martin Taylor said on Tuesday the bank was looking for the most appropriate way to return excess capital to shareholders.
Earlier, Barclays said it intended to return 500 million stg over the next twelve months, thus severing the link that has grown between its share repurchases and the publication of its results.
Barclays last year returned 780 million stg by way of two share repurchases.
"We're looking at what the most appropriate way of doing it will be, including what we have done in the past," Taylor told Reuters in an interview.

Asked whether Barclays was considering the payment of a special dividend as opposed to buying shares in the market, Taylor said, "A special dividend goes to all shareholders whether they want it or not and although it gives tax benefits to some gross funds, it imposes tax costs on others."
Taylor said that any special dividend payment would have to take into account the tax position of the shareholders as well as the company.
Taylor said that previous buybacks had been done for the benefit of those that do not sell their shares back.

"They allow non-sellers to concentrate their position," Taylor added. "I think what would happen if we did a conventional buy-back as we have done in the past is that we would have different classes of shareholders selling to us. It might be net funds, not gross funds."
